clue.text: Where all the goods will be sold out

definitions.text: Where all the goods will be sold out

parts.words: Where all the goods will be sold out
parts.note: sold out reads as every item gone, but means sold out of doors, under the sky rather than in a shop

explanation.walkthrough: 'Sold out' suggests stock exhausted; read it as sold outside, in the fresh air.
explanation.definitionFit: A street trading place with stalls in the open is where goods are sold outdoors.

clue.text: Pious rogue or one mounted in a ring

parts.note: PI is a crossword abbreviation for pious
a cad is a rogue or bounder

explanation.surface: A sanctimonious scoundrel, or perhaps a rider in a circus ring.
explanation.walkthrough: The ring is a bullring: this horseman goads the bull with a lance.
explanation.definitionFit: A bullfighter on horseback who lances the bull performs in the bullring.

clue.text: It may be proper for a sister to admit nothing

indicators.note: to admit is to let in, so the sister takes the next piece inside her

parts.note: a nun is a religious sister
O is the figure zero, nothing

explanation.surface: A remark on what is seemly for a nun to confess.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Proper' looks like a matter of propriety; it is grammar, as in a proper name for a person or place.
explanation.definitionFit: A word naming a particular person or place is a proper example of this part of speech.

clue.text: Breathe fire

definitions.meaning: to draw air into the lungs, the old physical sense
to fire someone is to stir them with enthusiasm

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both to inhale and to rouse with enthusiasm.

clue.text: Dull hack? No, an apostolic writer!

parts.note: matt means dull, without shine
to hew is to hack or chop

explanation.surface: Is that a tedious journalist? Not at all, it is one of the evangelists.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hack' pretends to be a jobbing journalist; it is the verb to chop.
explanation.definitionFit: The first Gospel is attributed to this apostle, one of the four evangelists.

clue.text: Bank gives free change

indicators.note: change tells us to alter the order of the letters of free

explanation.surface: A bank offering free small coins.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bank' and 'change' suggest money; the bank is a ridge under the sea.
explanation.definitionFit: A ridge of rock or coral near the surface of the sea is a sandbank of a kind.

clue.text: Takes parents out

indicators.note: out here means put out of order, so the letters of parents are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone escorting their mother and father on an outing.
explanation.definitionFit: To catch in a trap is to take, as a hunter takes game.

clue.text: Baby's rattle-could be dangerous

parts.note: the rattle is not a toy but the rasping sound in a child's chest from an infectious illness

explanation.walkthrough: A baby's rattle suggests a toy; here it is the noise of an illness in the chest.
explanation.definitionFit: Pertussis is a childhood infection with a gasping cough, serious in infants.

clue.text: It holds up communication when you contact someone in Warsaw

parts.note: to telegraph someone is to contact them by wire
a Pole is a native of Poland, whose capital is Warsaw

explanation.surface: Something that delays your message when you try to reach a person in Poland.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Holds up' suggests delay; it means physically supporting the wires.
explanation.definitionFit: A tall post carrying wires literally supports the lines that carry messages.

clue.text: Here Roman vessels made spasmodic attacks

parts.note: hic is the Latin for here, the Romans' word
cups are drinking vessels

explanation.surface: Roman ships launching fitful raids from this spot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Vessels' suggests ships; they are drinking cups.
explanation.definitionFit: Involuntary spasms of the diaphragm come in sudden fits.

clue.text: Apollo, for example, has wings and flies

definitions.meaning: the Apollo is a well-known London playhouse
a stage has wings at the sides and flies, the space above for hanging scenery

explanation.walkthrough: Apollo suggests the god or a rocket, and wings and flies a bird or insect; all are stage terms.
explanation.definitionFit: A playhouse such as London's Apollo has side wings and overhead flies for scenery.

clue.text: Matters of give and take between our betters

definitions.text: Matters of give and take between our betters

parts.words: Matters of give and take between our betters
parts.note: our betters sounds like our superiors, but they are people who place bets, and the give and take is offering and accepting prices

explanation.walkthrough: 'Our betters' looks like social superiors; read it as people who bet.
explanation.definitionFit: Bookmakers give prices and punters take them, so betting prices pass between gamblers.

clue.text: Fifty knocked out of the squadron in battle

indicators.note: knocked out of says one piece is removed from the other

parts.note: a flight is a unit of an air force, part of a squadron
L is the Roman numeral for fifty

explanation.surface: Fifty airmen lost from the squadron during combat.
explanation.definitionFit: A fight is a combat or battle.

clue.text: Cut in two, we hear

indicators.note: we hear tells us the word is judged by its spoken sound

parts.note: a pair is two of something

explanation.surface: An instruction to slice something into halves.
explanation.definitionFit: To pare is to trim or cut away the outer part.

clue.text: Getting a horse into a ship poses unexpected difficulties

indicators.note: into places the horse inside the ship

parts.note: SS is short for steamship
a nag is an old horse

explanation.surface: Loading a horse aboard a vessel causes trouble.
explanation.definitionFit: Snags are unforeseen problems or hitches.

clue.text: Happen to come later

explanation.definitionFit: The verb means both to occur as a result and to follow on afterwards.

clue.text: Possibly nearing the position a target is in danger

definitions.text: the position a target is in danger

indicators.note: possibly says the letters of nearing may be arranged another way

explanation.surface: Getting closer, perhaps, to where a target becomes vulnerable.
explanation.definitionFit: A target within reach of the guns is in danger of being hit.

clue.text: Family house in Berkshire

parts.note: the family is the British royal house, which shares its name with its castle home in Berkshire, a county west of London

explanation.walkthrough: It reads like a property advert; the family is the royal one and the house both its dynasty and its castle.
explanation.definitionFit: The British royal dynasty takes its name from its castle and town west of London.

clue.text: Where to find the greatest urbanity in Scotland

definitions.text: Where to find the greatest urbanity in Scotland

parts.words: Where to find the greatest urbanity in Scotland
parts.note: urbanity usually means polished manners, but here it is city-ness: the largest city in Scotland

explanation.walkthrough: 'Urbanity' suggests refinement; read it as being urban, so the biggest city.
explanation.definitionFit: Scotland's largest city is the most urban place in the country.

clue.text: He has main control of his craft

definitions.text: He has main control of his craft

parts.words: He has main control of his craft
parts.note: main means the sea and craft his ships, so this is a naval commander

explanation.walkthrough: 'Main control' sounds like chief control; the main is the open sea, and craft are vessels.
explanation.definitionFit: A senior naval officer commands a fleet at sea.

clue.text: Strange growth a person may see on safari

indicators.note: strange suggests the letters of growth and a are put in an odd new order

explanation.surface: An odd lump that a tourist might notice in the African bush.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Growth' reads as a lump on the skin, aptly; the definition is loose, meaning something a person may see on safari.
explanation.definitionFit: This tusked wild pig of the African savannah is a common sight for tourists in the bush.

clue.text: Rise to show appreciation

definitions.meaning: appreciation in value is a rise, as of investments

explanation.walkthrough: 'Appreciation' suggests gratitude; it is the financial sense, growth in value.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrasal verb means to increase steadily, which is how an asset appreciates.

clue.text: It reminds chaps to give me top priority

indicators.note: top priority says the word me goes first, ahead of the chaps

parts.note: men are chaps
taken as written

explanation.surface: A keepsake telling the men to put the speaker first.
explanation.definitionFit: A souvenir or keepsake serves as a reminder of a person or event.

clue.text: A furious pet

parts.note: pet here is not an animal but an old word for a sulk or fit of pique, and this one is furious

explanation.walkthrough: 'Pet' suggests an angry animal; it is the old sense of a fit of temper.
explanation.definitionFit: A violent outburst of bad temper is a furious sulk.

clue.text: Some resistance over taxing demands

definitions.meaning: the initials of On Her Majesty's Service are printed at the top of official British government letters such as tax bills

explanation.walkthrough: 'Over' means printed at the head of; the initials stand for On Her Majesty's Service, on official British government post.
explanation.definitionFit: These are units of electrical resistance, and the initials stamped on British official mail such as tax demands.

clue.text: Dirt, for example, left round the edge

indicators.note: round says the reversed piece encloses the edge
left means read leftwards, so the letters of for example are written backwards

parts.note: a rim is an edge

explanation.surface: Dirt left on the rim, like a ring around a bath.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Left' looks like 'remaining'; in an across clue it means written leftwards, so EG becomes GE, and 'round' wraps that around the edge.
explanation.definitionFit: Grime is ingrained dirt.

clue.text: Matches are always exciting in this game

definitions.text: Matches are always exciting in this game

parts.words: Matches are always exciting in this game
parts.note: matches looks like sporting contests, but in this card game a match is two cards of the same value, which brings the cry that ends a round

explanation.walkthrough: 'Matches' suggests fixtures; in this children's card game matching cards cause a shout.
explanation.definitionFit: In this card game players shout when two matching cards appear, which is always exciting.

clue.text: I'm in a new car

indicators.note: new says the letters of I'm in are given a fresh arrangement

explanation.surface: Someone boasting that they are inside a brand-new car.
explanation.definitionFit: The small British car is the classic example, made famous in the 1960s.

clue.text: It's in poor taste to let it stand

indicators.note: in says the answer is lodged inside the run of letters in poor taste to

explanation.surface: Leaving a crude remark in place would be tasteless.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In poor taste' reads as an idiom about vulgarity; 'in' is the signal and the letters sit across 'taste to'. The answer is the proof-reader's Latin mark.
explanation.definitionFit: Printers' Latin instructs that a crossed-out word should remain as it was.

clue.text: Sharing out with relish

indicators.note: out here means put out of its order, so the letters of sharing are rearranged

explanation.surface: Dividing up food with great enjoyment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'With relish' looks like enthusiasm; relish is the noun, a savoury accompaniment.
explanation.definitionFit: A decoration or accompaniment to food is a kind of relish.

clue.text: It's expected to be unaffected

definitions.meaning: a ... outcome is the one to be expected
a ... manner is unaffected and sincere

explanation.definitionFit: The adjective describes both what is normal and to be anticipated, and a manner free from pretence.

clue.text: Nobody's late so there's no need to hurry

explanation.definitionFit: Literally everyone arrived punctually; as an idiom, a reassurance that something will happen eventually without rushing.
